sections.heading: Why Distributive conditional types and pitfalls matters in production

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **Distributive conditional types and pitfalls** beyond one-line definitions. Production failures here look like silent data corruption, memory growth, type errors at CI, or async ordering bugs — not syntax errors. If you know JavaScript, use the comparison table to transfer intuition instead of memorizing rules in isolation.

blocks.title: Interview trap
blocks.body: Interviewers ask "Distributive conditional types and pitfalls" as a follow-up to system design or debugging exercises. They want mechanism, tradeoffs, and a concrete failure you have seen — not textbook definitions.

blocks.body: Treating Distributive conditional types and pitfalls as pure syntax without compile-time or run-time behavior. Skipping validation at API/JSON boundaries. Ignoring strict compiler flags differences. Hand-waving in design review without a test or metric.

blocks.text: Prove mastery of **Distributive conditional types and pitfalls** with a failing test that captures the edge case, a DevTools or heap snapshot showing the bug, and a clear tradeoff statement in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the compiler and emitted JS actually do — plus when the simple explicit version beats the clever abstraction.
